newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 23.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 23.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - Spending on advertising in western Europe is likely to rise by 4.9 percent in 1997 compared with 1996, according to the annual Europub review published by French communications group Havas. (Reuter)

PARIS - French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis says the partial privatisation of France Telecom has been delayed because of the French snap election, to avoid confusion between election publicity and the advertising campaign for the telecommunications group's privatisation. (Reuter)
PARIS - Jean-Marie Messier, chairman of Compagnie Generale des

Eaux (CGE), with an eye to the welfare of his new advertising unit Havas Advertising, is said to be unhappy that another CGE subsidiary, mobile phone firm SFR, still does its advertising through rival ad agency Carat. (Le Figaro)
MEDIA:

PARIS - The Cannes film festival celebrates its 50th birthday next month with a thriller-heavy competition slate, organisers say. Festival supremo Gilles Jacob says Golden Palm candidates at the May 7-18 jamboree include Johnny Depp ("The Brave") and Gary Oldman ("Nil By Mouth"), both first-timers in directing, and Wim Wenders ("The End of Violence") and Nick Cassavetes ("Call It Love"). (Reuter)

PARIS - Grundy France, a subsidiary of Pearson Television, launches FBG Films, a French company specialising in the production of fiction films for television, the first phase of a strategic development plan for Grundy and Pearson in France. (Reuter)

PARIS - Antoine Gallimard, chairman of French publishing house Gallimard, says he will allow Banque Nationale de Paris to sell the 12.5 percent of Gallimard it has held since 1990, and does not exclude allowing outsiders to take a stake in certain subsidiaries. (Les Echos)

PARIS - Television, the new monthly magazine launched this month by former Canal Plus chairman Andre Rousselet, has only sold 65,000 copies of its first issue, while the breakeven point comes at 140,000 sales.(Liberation)
PARIS - The French Senate, due to give a second reading to a broadcasting bill from May 5, has suspended the reading until after the French Parliamentary elections. (Liberation)

PARIS - Hachette Filipacchi Medias, formed from the merger of Filipacchi Medias et Hachette Filipacchi Presse, hopes to make operating profit of one billion francs in 1999. It had pro-forma operating profit of 795 million francs in 1996. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BRUSSELS - Workers from French carmaker Renault's doomed plant at Vilvoorde in Belgium plan to demonstrate in northern France on Thursday, Belga news agency says, citing union sources. They will head to Lille, hoping to meet French Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin, and plan to ask him to keep the plant open if his party wins the elections, says one union source. (Reuter)
TOKYO - Honda Motor Co Ltd says it is studying whether to take a stake in the Sino-French Guanzhou Peugeot Automobile joint venture. (Reuter)
LONDON - Goldman Sachs investment bank cuts its earnings
estimates for French carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen following
disappointing results last week. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

PARIS - Jean-Pierre Vittu de Keraoul, chairman of France's regional press association Federation Nationale de la Presse Periodique Regionale, is elected chairman of the national press body Federation Nationale de la Presse Francaise, succeeding Bernard Porte. (Le Figaro)
PARIS - Jean-Francois Meaudre, Havas co-deputy managing
director, is leaving the board of Havas four months after Havas's deal with Compagnie Generale des Eaux. (Les Echos) ***********************************************
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
